Thread 1/6 🧵

There’s a lot of buzz around Tesla’s new Roadster, and I must say, it was fascinating to watch a car jump over other vehicles and manoeuvre in mid-air.

But is it really as revolutionary as people are claiming? I have a few questions.

2/6 — Is it the first car to jump or fly?

No.

In 2025, China’s BYD demonstrated its Yangwang U9 jumping over obstacles at 120 km/h, covering more than 6 metres.

And flying cars aren’t new either. The Fulton Airphibian was flying back in the 1940s.

Tesla’s technology is different, but the concept isn’t entirely new.

3/6 — Is it the fastest car?

Not in terms of top speed.

Tesla claims over 370 km/h, while BYD’s Yangwang U9 Xtreme reached 496.22 km/h in 2025.

However, Tesla’s demonstrated 0–60 mph acceleration of around 0.81 seconds is definitely impressive.

4/6 — Does it actually fly?

From what we’ve seen, it jumps over a few cars, manoeuvres in mid-air and lands.

That’s impressive engineering, but it’s not sustained flight. We haven’t seen it fly over long distances or remain airborne for an extended period.

Calling it a flying car might be a little premature.

Businesses do not suffer because of peaceful protests. They suffer when the govt decides to shut down an entire city, suspend internet services and restrict the movement of its own citizens and turn the city into a war-zone. 

Since its inception, the Cockroach Janta Party has maintained that we will always follow Gandhi’s path of peace and non-violence, and we have stood by that commitment. We have organised protests in Mumbai, Pune, Jaipur, Lucknow, Bengaluru and Nagpur, and every single one of them has been peaceful. I was personally assaulted in Jaipur, but even then, I chose not to retaliate because responding to violence with violence goes against everything we believe in. We would rather exercise the rights guaranteed to us by the Constitution, drafted under the leadership of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, than resort to physical force. Our strength comes from our commitment to constitutional values, and no amount of provocation will make us abandon them.

Despite this, there are constant attempts to portray us as anarchists simply because we refuse to remain silent. But demanding answers from the govt is not anarchy, protesting against injustice on the streets is not anarchy, and questioning those who hold public office is certainly not anarchy. These are the most fundamental expressions of democracy. The very party that is in power today spent decades organising protests, taking to the streets and questioning the governments of the day when it was in opposition. Had the same restrictions, intimidation and police crackdowns been used against them, many of those who occupy positions of power today might never have reached where they are. It is deeply hypocritical to celebrate protests as a democratic right when you are in opposition and treat the same act as a threat to public order when you come to power.

We are not asking for privileges or special treatment. We are simply asking to exercise the rights that belong to every citizen of this Republic, irrespective of which party is in power. So let us fulfil our duty as citizens of this country by questioning those we elect, demanding accountability and speaking up whenever we witness injustice. 

A govt that has been elected by the people is bound to listen to the people, not silence them. Democracy does not end once the votes have been counted.

This is how these influencers fool their audience 🙏🥲
